title: Robust distortion riskmetrics under Wasserstein ambiguity
abstract: arXiv:2610.09622v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Risk evaluation under distributional ambiguity is central to decision making in finance, economics, and operations research. Wasserstein balls provide a natural way to describe uncertainty around a reference distribution. We solve a natural yet open problem of robust optimization for the class of distortion riskmetrics with Wasserstein distance as the sole ambiguity constraint. This chosen objective class does not require convexity, monotonicity, and continuity of distortion functions, encompassing many common risk measures and deviation measures. First, we characterize conditions under which direct convexification preserves the worst-case value. Second, we develop a constructive method for exact worst-case evaluation when the direct convexification conditions fail. tldr: 该论文解决了以Wasserstein距离为唯一模糊约束的失真风险度量类的鲁棒优化这一开放问题，且不要求失真函数具有凸性、单调性或连续性，提出了直接凸化保持最坏情形值的条件、精确最坏情形评估的构造性方法以及带有可计算误差界的显式近似最坏情形分布。
en_tdlr: The paper solves the open problem of robust optimization for distortion riskmetrics under Wasserstein distance as the sole ambiguity constraint—without requiring convexity, monotonicity, or continuity of distortion functions—by characterizing direct convexification conditions, developing a constructive exact worst-case evaluation method, and constructing explicit approximate worst-case distributions with computable error bounds.
